chunks: “We used to forbid people from taking the meat of sacrificial animals out of Minā after three days due to the scarcity of meat and the large number of people. But today, the meat has become abundant, and the people have decreased, so there is no harm in taking it out.”

key_terms.الْأَضَاحِيِّ: the sacrificial animals offered during hajj
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the hajj site where sacrificial rites are performed

ai.seo_question: Why was taking sacrificial meat out of Minā after three days once forbidden and later allowed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explains that the earlier prohibition on removing sacrificial meat from Minā after three days was based on circumstances of need and crowding. Since those conditions changed and meat became abundant, the ruling no longer posed a problem, showing attention to context in legal application.
